Tip resistance (`tip_resistance_mohm`) climbs steadily over hours from about 0.15 mOhm towards the 0.185 mOhm alarm limit as the tip faces pick up coating material and oxide (which raises contact resistance) and lose their shape, while the current stepper raises weld current (`weld_current_ka`) to compensate. Rejects at ST60 follow later, once the weld nuggets become undersized. Servo temperature, gun air pressure and cycle time stay normal.
Tip resistance that rises in a straight line over several hours, together with a stepping weld current, is the signature of electrode tip wear, not of a controller fault.

If tip resistance rises at one weld cell only, the tips or the tip dresser at that cell are the cause; if weld faults start at ST20 right after a press changeover, check the parts first (see Section 6.7).
